scorecard.rationale: Oral curcumin improved mean open-field speed or timed pole descent in independent Parkinson-model rodent comparisons. The standardized turmeric-root curcumin abstract adds broader motor and memory outcomes in a separate rat model with no verified speed endpoint. The older-adult registry reported 0.089 m/s less walking-speed gain with curcumin than placebo in 17 participants and no between-arm analysis. Human Parkinson carrier studies supply composite motor scores. The closely matched animal timing outcomes retain a minimal easing signal while culinary ground turmeric and separate clinical bradykinesia remain unresolved. The FXTAS clinical review describes patient-perceived benefit for a broad list of dietary options including turmeric. It does not identify the specific options, ground turmeric exposure, or a bradykinesia comparison. Its motor assessment citation concerns a separate study.
